question: X6, Menu pulled in to its 6-column floor on a phone, with the pointer stopping at the floor or going past it; and whether the timing lags of CAP-X6PHONEROWS.json settle after 2 s. Predictions pushed before the read of CAP-X6FARSETTLE.json.
setup: Blocks Probe, unsaved, a new section. Menu added on desktop and viewed on the phone at 8 columns (28 rows, 1/2/29/10). Each pull is undone before the next. Pulls of 96 px (2 columns, the pointer stops at the floor) and 150 px (3.1 columns, past it) from each side; a pull to 7 columns then 200 px more; a 300 px pull read while held and let go. Then Instagram and OpenTable pulled in one column at a time to their floors and out again, each step read at 400 ms and again 2 s later. Then a new OpenTable pulled 500 px in one pull.
rule: Refit (the phone rule's last refit, CAP-X6PHONEROWS.json): a side pull on a phone gives max(rows before, ceil((h + 11) / 35 - g)), h the content's height at the landed width. g is 0.13 when the pointer stops at or above the floor, and 0.02 (no give) when the pointer goes past the floor, so the snapped width would be under it. Menu at 6 columns is 1077.2 high: 31.09 rows, so 31 at the floor and 32 past it (CAP-X6PHONEFLOORS.json's two far pulls read 32; CAP-X6PHONEROWS.json's step to 6 read 31).

predictions.case: Menu e 7 then 200 px past floor
Menu let go past floor (300 px)

predictions.predict: not predicted: the question for the lead is whether they settle to ours, ceil((h + 11) / 35 - 0.13) for Instagram, and max(rows before, that) for OpenTable

score: Counted on the seven Menu and OpenTable far cases above, at their 400 ms reads. The rule is frozen with this file: whatever the count, it stands, and misses are named.
